guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Paediatric Basic Life Support 2021
title: Child cardiac arrest at a school sports day
setting: School sports day. 9-year-old child collapsed during a race. Lying still on the track, pale, unresponsive, and not breathing.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive and not breathing normally. Paediatric cardiac arrest is a critical life-threatening emergency. Unequivocally sick: start CPR beginning with rescue breaths.

shared.danger: Spectators and runners ongoing near track

history.history: Reported feeling unwell before the race, collapsed 200m in
history.additional: Teacher is on scene and is a trained paediatric first aider

followUp.question: What is the correct resuscitation sequence for this 9-year-old child?

options.text: Give 5 initial rescue breaths, then 15 compressions to 2 breaths, and fetch the AED
Perform adult CPR (30 compressions to 2 breaths) starting with compressions
Place in the recovery position and splash cold water on the face
Check for a pulse for 2 minutes before starting any intervention

followUp.explanation: Paediatric arrest is usually hypoxic, so resuscitation begins with 5 initial rescue breaths followed by a 15:2 ratio of compressions to breaths. Adult BLS ratio of 30:2 is secondary if paediatric protocol is not known.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Start paediatric CPR immediately. Paediatric sequence is 5 breaths, then 15:2.
levelFlags.erNotes: Prioritize airway and ventilations with high-flow oxygen, attach paediatric pads to AED if available (or adult pads if >8 years old), and coordinate with the teacher on scene.
